   ---------------------------

- Fix: the 7.11.1 changes meant that conflicts between a requested measurement
  core and other settings would raise an error. This was a breaking change from
  previous behavior, as reported in `issue 2076`_ and `issue 2078`_.

  The previous behavior has been restored: when the requested core conflicts
  with other settings, another core is used instead, and a warning is issued.

- For contributors: the repo has moved from Ned's `nedbat GitHub account`_ to
  the `coveragepy GitHub organization`_. The default branch has changed from
  master to main.

.. _issue 2076: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2076
.. _issue 2078: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2078

.. _coveragepy GitHub organization: https://github.com/coveragepy


.. _changes_7-11-2:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.11.2
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: using the "sysmon" measurement core in 7.11.1, if Python code was
  claimed to come from a non-Python file, a ``NotPython`` exception could be
  raised. This could happen for example with Jinja templates compiled to
  Python, as reported in `issue 2077`_. This is now fixed.

- Doc: corrected the first entry in the 7.11.1 changelog.

.. _issue 2077: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2077


.. _changes_7-11-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.11.1
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: some chanages to details of how the measurement core is chosen, and how
  conflicting settings are handled. The "sysmon" core cannot be used with some
  conurrency settings, with dynamic context, and in Python 3.12/3.13, with
  branch measurement.

  - If the core is not specified and defaults to "sysmon" (Python 3.14+), but
    other settings conflict with sysmon, then the "ctrace" core will be used
    instead with no warning. For concurrency conflicts, this used to produce an
    error, as described in `issue 2064`_.

  - If the "sysmon" core is explicitly requested in your configuration, but
    other settings conflict, an error is now raised. This used to produce a
    warning.

- Fix: some multi-line case clauses or for loops (and probably other
  constructs) could cause incorrect claims of missing branches with the
  sys.monitoring core, as described in `issue 2070`_. This is now fixed.

- Fix: when running in pytest under coverage, a ``breakpoint()`` would stop in
  the wrong frame, one level down from where it should, as described in `issue
  1420`_. This was due to a coverage change in v6.4.1 that seemed to give a
  slight performance improvement, but I couldn't reproduce the performance
  gain, so it's been reverted, fixing the debugger problem.

- A new debug option ``--debug=core`` shows which core is in use and why.

- Split ``sqlite`` debugging information out of the ``sys`` :ref:`coverage
  debug <cmd_debug>` and :ref:`cmd_run_debug` options since it's bulky and not
  very useful.

- Updated the :ref:`howitworks` page to better describe the three different
  measurement cores.

body:
Related PRs/issues: [Jira TP1-3345](https://mozilla-hub.atlassian.net/browse/TP1-3345) / https://github.com/MozillaFoundation/foundation.mozilla.org/issues/14928
Review app: https://foundation-s-tp1-3345-d-4jeojl.mofostaging.net/en/


# Description

Fixes Safari-specific rendering bug where sticky donate banner (e.g., the pushdown version) appears above nav and main content when scrolling. Safari's sticky element rendering doesn't respect z-index values from other elements.

**The fix**: Implemented JS workaround for Safari using extreme 3D transforms to force proper layer separation

# Approaches That Didn't Work

I tried the following approaches but none worked:

1. **CSS transform on all elements** - Broke nav dropdown positioning (transforms create new containing blocks)
2. **z-index: -1 on banner** - Made banner non-interactive (e.g., buttons couldn't be clicked)
3. **Wrapper elements** - Interfered with sticky positioning calculations
4. **Simple z-index changes via JS** - Safari still ignored them
5. **Small translateZ values** - Not enough 3D separation to override Safari's rendering
6. **Fixed positioning instead of sticky** - Changed the desired UX behavior

# To Test Locally

1. Check out this branch and run it
2. Set up a Pushdown Donate Banner
3. Test on Safari to see the bug mentioned in the Jira ticket is resolved.

body:
# Description

This pull request adds support for custom template-based output formatting to the Azure Storage Queue reaction using Handlebars templates with per-query configuration. This provides maximum flexibility for integrating with downstream systems that expect specific message formats.

## Changes Made

### Reaction Implementation
- **Added Handlebars.Net dependency** (version 2.1.6) to enable template-based message formatting
- **Created new components:**
  - `QueryConfig.cs` - Model for per-query template configuration with distinct templates for added, updated, and deleted change types, with JsonPropertyName attributes for proper YAML deserialization
  - `ITemplateFormatter.cs` - Interface for template formatting operations with separate methods for each change type
  - `TemplateFormatter.cs` - Implementation using Handlebars templates with performance optimizations (template caching)
  - `OutputFormat.cs` - Shared enum containing Packed, Unpacked, and Template format options
- **Updated existing components:**
  - `ChangeHandler.cs` - Extended to support Template format with per-query distinct templates for each change type
  - `ControlSignalHandler.cs` - Updated to handle Template format (skips control signals when using template format)
  - `Program.cs` - Registered TemplateFormatter and configured typed QueryConfig with YAML deserialization
  - `storagequeue-reaction.csproj` - Added Handlebars.Net package reference and excluded test files from compilation
  - `default-reaction-providers.yaml` - Updated StorageQueue reaction provider to include "template" in the format enum
  - `Makefile` - Updated test target to run `dotnet test`
  - `storagequeue-reaction.sln` - Added test project to solution
- **Enhanced documentation:**
  - Updated README.md with comprehensive Template format documentation showing YAML format with pipe block scalar notation for query configurations
  - Added example configurations demonstrating per-query template usage with clean YAML structure
  - Documented available context variables for each template type

### Testing
- **Added unit tests:**
  - Created `StorageQueue.Tests` project with xUnit testing framework
  - Comprehensive test coverage for TemplateFormatter with 14 unit tests
  - Tests cover template formatting for added, updated, and deleted operations
  - Tests verify JSON element handling, template caching, and conditional logic
  - All tests passing (14/14)

## Template Features

The template format uses per-query configuration following the HTTP reaction pattern. Each query can define distinct Handlebars templates for different change types:

- **Added template**: Access to `after` context (new state of the result)
- **Updated template**: Access to `before` and `after` contexts (previous and new states)
- **Deleted template**: Access to `before` context (previous state of the result)

Templates use standard Handlebars syntax with support for conditionals, iteration, and all standard Handlebars helpers.

**Configuration Format**: Query configurations are provided as YAML strings using the pipe block scalar notation (`|`) in the reaction manifest. Each query uses the format `query-name: |` followed by the YAML content containing an object with `added`, `updated`, and `deleted` properties. Multi-line template strings use YAML's pipe notation for clean, readable formatting without escape characters. The implementation uses JsonPropertyName attributes to map YAML property names to C# model properties during deserialization.

**Note:** Template format is not supported for control signals. Control signals will be skipped when using template format.

## Testing

- ✅ Reaction project builds successfully with no errors
- ✅ Security checks pass with no vulnerabilities detected
- ✅ Implementation follows established patterns from HTTP reaction and other reactions
- ✅ Reaction provider YAML validated successfully
- ✅ Unit tests added with comprehensive coverage (14 tests, all passing)
- ✅ Tests can be run with `make test` or `dotnet test`
- ✅ YAML deserialization validated with unit tests

## Type of change

- This pull request adds or changes features of Drasi and has an approved issue (issue link required).

Fixes: #issue_number

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> In this repo, under https://github.com/drasi-project/drasi-platform/tree/main/reactions, there are a number of reaction components for the drasi platform. Currently, the Azure Storage queue reaction, which is located here:
> 
> https://github.com/drasi-project/drasi-platform/tree/main/reactions/azure/storagequeue-reaction
> 
> Outputs messages to queues in either "packed" or "unpacked" format. I would like to add a third custom format, that uses handlebars templates, call it "template" format. There is an example of a reaction using handlebars templates here:
> 
> https://github.com/drasi-project/drasi-platform/tree/main/reactions/http
> 
> Although it is a node.js implementation and the storage queue reaction is written in .net
> 
> An appropriate library for implementing the handlebars templating engine should be used rather than reinventing the wheel.

This pull request introduces several improvements and fixes to the onboarding flow, UI responsiveness, and local storage management, as well as some infrastructure updates. The onboarding process now uses more robust local storage keys, persists state across reloads, and handles corrupted data gracefully. The navigation UI is improved for better loading feedback, and the onboarding logic is more consistent and maintainable.

**Onboarding Flow & State Management:**

* Introduced dedicated localStorage keys for onboarding steps, assistant messages, and selected nudges, ensuring onboarding state persists across reloads and is cleaned up properly when onboarding completes or is skipped. body:
Adds a new GitHub Actions workflow that builds executables for pull requests, addressing issue #5. The implementation uses a reusable workflow to share code between PR and release builds, ensuring consistency and maintainability.

## Changes Made

- **New PR CI Workflow**: Created `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml` that triggers on pull request events (opened, synchronize, reopened)
- **Reusable Workflow**: Created `.github/workflows/build-executables-reusable.yml` containing shared build logic that both PR and release workflows call
- **GUI Launch Tests**: Added `tests/test_executable_gui_launch.py` to verify built executables can launch and open a GUI window
- **GUI Verification**: Test verifies the GUI actually opens by checking if the shell server on port 40405 responds (this server starts when the main window is created)
- **Fixed Permissions**: Reusable workflow inherits permissions from the calling workflow, allowing PR workflow with read-only permissions to work

## Implementation Details

- Uses matrix strategy to build on both `ubuntu-latest` and `windows-latest`
- Builds executables using PyInstaller with the same configuration as the publish workflow
- Uploads the `dist/` directory directly as artifacts (GitHub Actions handles compression)
- Runs GUI launch tests on both Linux (using xvfb for headless display) and Windows
- Timeouts are configurable via environment variables (GUI_TEST_STARTUP_TIMEOUT, GUI_TEST_TERMINATION_TIMEOUT)

## Testing

- ✅ No security vulnerabilities detected by CodeQL
- ✅ Workflow syntax is valid
- ✅ Follows existing patterns from publish workflow
- ✅ GUI launch test verifies application opens successfully by checking shell server response

Thanks for asking me to work on this. I will get started on it and keep this PR's description up to date as I form a plan and make progress.


<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

Implement the behavior described in issue #43: UI and Health module: Auto-reinitialize devices and clarify unavailable device states.

Context:
- Repository: agster27/HeatTrax_Tapo_M400_Scheduler
- The scheduler manages Tapo/Kasa devices in groups, with Device Health and Device Control in the Web UI.
- Current behavior: If a device is offline during startup, initialization fails (e.g., "Timed out getting discovery response"), the group ends up with 0 active devices, and the Web UI Device Control shows "No devices configured or available". Once the device later comes online, the system does not automatically rediscover or reinitialize it; users must restart the container.
- Health checks run periodically (default every 24 hours) but do not yet trigger reinitialization that repopulates Device Control in this scenario.

Requirements (derived from issue #43 and prior discussion, with screenshots like ![image1](image1)):
1. Health-check-driven auto reinitialization
   - Extend the health check system so that when it detects a previously-unreachable or uninitialized device has become reachable, it triggers reinitialization of that device (and its group) without requiring a full process restart.
   - After successful reinitialization, Device Control and Device Health should treat the device as active, and the device_group_manager should report it in status calls.
   - Ensure this works per-device/per-group and integrates cleanly with existing EnhancedScheduler and DeviceGroupManager logic.

2. Clear distinction between configured vs active devices in Web UI
   - In the Health page Device Control section, replace the generic "No devices configured or available" message with more informative messaging that distinguishes between:
     a) No devices configured at all.
     b) Devices configured but 0 active (due to initialization/connection failures).
   - Show counts like "Configured: N, Active: M" somewhere in the Device Control area (or near the list) using data provided by the backend.

3. Improved Device Health cards for unreachable devices
   - Update the Device Health UI to clearly indicate when a device is unreachable or failed to initialize.
   - For such devices, show a status like "unreachable (last error: <message>)" and/or "initialization failed" rather than just showing `Current State: off` as if that were live data.
   - If the backend already tracks last error per device/group, surface that via the API; if not, extend the device_group_manager / health_check layer to store a simple last_error string and expose it in the `/api/devices/status` or related endpoint used by the Health page.

4. API / backend enhancements
   - Ensure the JSON returned by the Web API endpoints used by the Health and Device Control views contains enough information to:
     - Distinguish configured vs active devices.
     - Identify devices that failed to initialize vs devices that are active but temporarily unreachable.
     - Include last_error (if any) and/or last_seen timestamps where appropriate.
   - Maintain backward compatibility: existing callers should not break; new fields should be additive.

5. UX and messaging
   - When there are configured devices but none are active, display guidance text in the UI such as:
     - "1 device configured but currently unavailable. Check power, network, and Tapo credentials." (pluralize for N>1)
   - Optionally expose a "Retry initialization" or "Re-scan devices" button that calls a new backend endpoint to force a reinitialization of device groups, with appropriate logging. If this is added, wire it to the UI in a simple, unobtrusive way.

6. Logging and observability
   - Add clear log messages when:
     - Health checks detect a previously failed device becoming reachable.
     - Automatic reinitialization attempts start and whether they succeed or fail.
     - Device Control status reports configured vs active counts.

7. Tests and documentation
   - Add or update unit tests and/or integration-style tests (if present in the repo) to cover:
     - Device offline at startup, then comes online, and health check triggers successful reinit.
     - Web API returns configured vs active counts and last_error fields.
   - Update README/SETUP or HEALTH_CHECK docs briefly to mention the auto-reinit behavior and the new UI messaging.

Implementation notes:
- Existing files likely to be touched: `device_group_manager.py`, `health_check.py`, `health_server.py`, `web_server.py`, possibly `state_manager.py` and any React/JS/HTML templates for the Health page.

Deliverables:

*This pull request was created as a result of the following prompt from Copilot chat.*
> Implement the behavior described in issue #43: UI and Health module: Auto-reinitialize devices and clarify unavailable device states.
> 
> Context:
> - Repository: agster27/HeatTrax_Tapo_M400_Scheduler
> - The scheduler manages Tapo/Kasa devices in groups, with Device Health and Device Control in the Web UI.
> - Current behavior: If a device is offline during startup, initialization fails (e.g., "Timed out getting discovery response"), the group ends up with 0 active devices, and the Web UI Device Control shows "No devices configured or available". Once the device later comes online, the system does not automatically rediscover or reinitialize it; users must restart the container.
> - Health checks run periodically (default every 24 hours) but do not yet trigger reinitialization that repopulates Device Control in this scenario.
> 
> Requirements (derived from issue #43 and prior discussion, with screenshots like ![image1](image1)):
> 1. Health-check-driven auto reinitialization
>    - Extend the health check system so that when it detects a previously-unreachable or uninitialized device has become reachable, it triggers reinitialization of that device (and its group) without requiring a full process restart.
>    - After successful reinitialization, Device Control and Device Health should treat the device as active, and the device_group_manager should report it in status calls.
>    - Ensure this works per-device/per-group and integrates cleanly with existing EnhancedScheduler and DeviceGroupManager logic.
> 
> 2. Clear distinction between configured vs active devices in Web UI
>    - In the Health page Device Control section, replace the generic "No devices configured or available" message with more informative messaging that distinguishes between:
>      a) No devices configured at all.
>      b) Devices configured but 0 active (due to initialization/connection failures).
>    - Show counts like "Configured: N, Active: M" somewhere in the Device Control area (or near the list) using data provided by the backend.
> 
> 3. Improved Device Health cards for unreachable devices
>    - Update the Device Health UI to clearly indicate when a device is unreachable or failed to initialize.
>    - For such devices, show a status like "unreachable (last error: <message>)" and/or "initialization failed" rather than just showing `Current State: off` as if that were live data.
>    - If the backend already tracks last error per device/group, surface that via the API; if not, extend the device_group_manager / health_check layer to store a simple last_error string and expose it in the `/api/devices/status` or related endpoint use

<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.12.0
   ```
   ---------------------------

- The HTML report now shows separate coverage totals for statements and
  branches, as well as the usual combined coverage percentage. Thanks to Ryuta
  Otsuka for the `discussion <issue 2081_>`_ and the `implementation
  <pull 2085_>`_.

- The JSON report now includes separate coverage totals for statements and
  branches, thanks to `Ryuta Otsuka <pull 2090_>`_.

- Fix: ``except*`` clauses were not handled properly under the "sysmon"
  measurement core, causing KeyError exceptions as described in `issue 2086`_.
  This is now fixed.

- Fix: we now defend against aggressive mocking of ``open()`` that could cause
  errors inside coverage.py.  An example of a failure is in `issue 2083`_.

- Fix: in unusual cases where a test suite intentionally exhausts the system's
  file descriptors to test handling errors in ``open()``, coverage.py would
  fail when trying to open source files, as described in `issue 2091`_.  This
  is now fixed.

- A small tweak to the HTML report: file paths now use thin spaces around
  slashes to make them easier to read.

.. _issue 2081: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2081
.. _issue 2083: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2083

.. _pull 2090: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2090

.. _changes_7-11-3:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.11.3
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: the 7.11.1 changes meant that conflicts between a requested measurement
  core and other settings would raise an error. This was a breaking change from
  previous behavior, as reported in `issue 2076`_ and `issue 2078`_.

  The previous behavior has been restored: when the requested core conflicts
  with other settings, another core is used instead, and a warning is issued.

- For contributors: the repo has moved from Ned's `nedbat GitHub account`_ to
  the `coveragepy GitHub organization`_. The default branch has changed from
  master to main.

.. _issue 2076: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2076
.. _issue 2078: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2078

.. _changes_7-11-2:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.11.2
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: using the "sysmon" measurement core in 7.11.1, if Python code was
  claimed to come from a non-Python file, a ``NotPython`` exception could be
  raised. This could happen for example with Jinja templates compiled to
  Python, as reported in `issue 2077`_. This is now fixed.

- Doc: corrected the first entry in the 7.11.1 changelog.

.. _issue 2077: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2077


.. _changes_7-11-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.11.1
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: some chanages to details of how the measurement core is chosen, and how
  conflicting settings are handled. The "sysmon" core cannot be used with some
  conurrency settings, with dynamic context, and in Python 3.12/3.13, with
  branch measurement.

  - If the core is not specified and defaults to "sysmon" (Python 3.14+), but
    other settings conflict with sysmon, then the "ctrace" core will be used
    instead with no warning. For concurrency conflicts, this used to produce an
    error, as described in `issue 2064`_.

  - If the "sysmon" core is explicitly requested in your configuration, but
    other settings conflict, an error is now raised. This used to produce a
    warning.

- Fix: some multi-line case clauses or for loops (and probably other
  constructs) could cause incorrect claims of missing branches with the
  sys.monitoring core, as described in `issue 2070`_. This is now fixed.

- Fix: when running in pytest under coverage, a ``breakpoint()`` would stop in
  the wrong frame, one level down from where it should, as described in `issue
  1420`_. This was due to a coverage change in v6.4.1 that seemed to give a
  slight performance improvement, but I couldn't reproduce the performance
  gain, so it's been reverted, fixing the debugger problem.

- A new debug option ``--debug=core`` shows which core is in use and why.

- Split ``sqlite`` debugging information out of the ``sys`` :ref:`coverage
  debug <cmd_debug>` and :ref:`cmd_run_debug` options since it's bulky and not
  very useful.

- Updated the :ref:`howitworks` page to better describe the three different
  measurement cores.

Implement foundational skills for Shannon v5.4, achieving feature parity
with superpowers framework while adding Shannon's quantitative metrics,
Serena MCP persistence, and hook enforcement patterns.

## New Skills (4 Production-Ready)

### Debugging Skills (skills/debugging/)
- **systematic-debugging**: 4-phase root cause investigation protocol
  * Phase 1: Root Cause Investigation (Sequential MCP, boundary diagnosis)
  * Phase 2: Pattern Analysis (working code comparison, similarity scores)
  * Phase 3: Hypothesis Testing (confidence scoring 0.00-1.00)
  * Phase 4: Implementation (NO MOCKS tests + defense-in-depth)
  * Iron Law: NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE FIRST
  * Serena persistence for pattern detection across sessions
  * Integrated with root-cause-tracing and defense-in-depth

- **root-cause-tracing**: Backward call chain tracing to find original trigger
  * 5-step process: Observe → Immediate → Caller → Trace Up → Trigger
  * Quantified trace depth metrics (shallow/medium/deep/very deep)
  * Instrumentation techniques for complex traces
  * Component boundary identification
  * Defense-in-depth application at source + all layers

### Testing Skills (skills/testing/)
- **defense-in-depth**: Multi-layer validation making bugs structurally impossible
  * 4-layer framework: Entry → Business Logic → Environment → Debug
  * Layer coverage scoring (0-4, target ≥3)
  * Validation redundancy scoring (target ≥2.0)
  * Bypass resistance testing (100% target)
  * NO MOCKS integration (Layer 3 enforces real systems)

### Collaboration Skills (skills/collaboration/)
- **verification-before-completion**: Evidence-based completion gates
  * 5-step gate: Identify → Run → Read → Verify → Claim
  * Red flag detection: "should", "probably", "seems to"
  * Hook enforcement design (post_tool_use.py integration)
  * Fresh evidence requirement (<5 minutes)
  * Serena evidence storage for audit trail

## Planning Documents

  * Gap analysis: Shannon vs superpowers

Introduce orbic-shell and tplink-shell utils which both launch telnet and connect to the device using a DIY telnet-like client. The idea here is that we make it easier for Windows users to connect even though they have neither telnet nor nc utilities and hide the internals of how "obtaining a shell" works from the user to some extent.

In that spirit of hiding implementation details, update documentation to remove mentions of tplink-start-telnet and orbic-start-telnet and fix some outdated docs for moxee too.

As a side effect this makes uninstallation generally simpler for network-installed devices, and generally more attainable for Windows users.

Fixes the mobile navigation menu toggle button that was not functioning due to a missing variable declaration in `shared-nav.html`.

## Problem

The mobile menu toggle button (☰) was not working in mobile view. When clicked, nothing happened because the `sidebar` variable was referenced in the `toggleSidebar()` function but was never declared.

## Solution

Added the missing `sidebar` variable declaration in `shared-nav.html`:

```javascript
const sidebar = document.getElementById('sidebar');
```

This minimal one-line fix ensures the sidebar element is properly referenced when the toggle button is clicked.

- Added `const sidebar = document.getElementById('sidebar');` at line 68 in `shared-nav.html`
- Variable is now properly declared alongside existing `menuToggle` and `sidebarBackdrop` declarations

- ✅ Sidebar closes properly with Escape key

author: hariprasadravi
body:
`torch.nn.Conv2d` with `padding = 'valid'` generates a `torch.ops.aten.conv2d.padding` op in ExportedProgram, which is later decomposed to  `torch.ops.aten.convolution.default` with a single padding value of `[0]` after running `ep.run_decompositions()`.

This causes a compiler failure in `torch-to-tosa` because the code expects padding to have two elements.

Here is the print of the `ExportedProgram`

```
>>> print(prog)
ExportedProgram:
    class GraphModule(torch.nn.Module):
        def forward(self, p_0_weight: "f32[1, 1, 1, 1]", p_0_bias: "f32[1]", input: "f32[1, 1, 5, 5]"):
            input_1 = input             
            conv2d: "f32[1, 1, 5, 5]" = torch.ops.aten.conv2d.padding(input_1, p_0_weight, p_0_bias);  input_1 = p_0_weight = p_0_bias = None
            return (conv2d,)
```
```            
>>> prog_decomposed = prog.run_decompositions()
>>> print(prog_decomposed)
ExportedProgram:
    class GraphModule(torch.nn.Module):
        def forward(self, p_0_weight: "f32[1, 1, 1, 1]", p_0_bias: "f32[1]", input: "f32[1, 1, 5, 5]"):
            input_1 = input
            convolution: "f32[1, 1, 5, 5]" = torch.ops.aten.convolution.default(input_1, p_0_weight, p_0_bias, [1, 1], [0], [1, 1], False, [0], 1);  input_1 = p_0_weight = p_0_bias = None
            return (convolution,)
```            
 
Note: A previous, correct decomposition for a similar issue exists and is locked down by e2e tests (refer to relevant context like #3883). This fix aligns the conv2d.padding decomposition with that correct behavior.

Since locking this specific decomposition down with end-to-end (e2e) tests was problematic, a dedicated LIT test has been added to the test suite to ensure this specific padding regression cannot reoccur.

author: rental-turbotenant
body:
# Network cost passthrough for platforms

Learn how to pass network costs from a platform to your connected accounts.

Network cost passthrough (IC++) is a capability for platforms to pass network costs through to their connected accounts. This allows you to offer IC+ pricing to your connected accounts instead of charging a blended rate for all card payments.

Stripe first charges network costs to your platform account. Within a few hours, we help you recover these costs from the connected account’s balance and add them to the platform’s balance, to ensure that the platform is fully compensated for the network costs. This includes all network cost adjustments related to network costs, including non-transactional scheme fees, refunds, and disputes.

## Manage network cost passthrough status for your connected accounts

If you created the connected account in Stripe and have access to the `stripe_account_id`, you can set new accounts as network cost passthrough or transition existing accounts to network cost passthrough.

### Set an account as network cost passthrough

To set an account as network cost passthrough, you must schedule a new Pricing Config Scheme object with the `network_costs` type using the [Pricing Config Scheme Create API](https://docs.stripe.com/api/pricing-config-scheme/create.md?api-version=preview):

```curl
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/pricing_configs/network_costs/schemes \
  -u "<<YOUR_SECRET_KEY>>:" \
  -H "Stripe-Version: 2025-07-30.preview; network_costs_private_preview=v1" \
  -H "Stripe-Account: {{CONNECTEDACCOUNT_ID}}" \
  -d enabled=true
```

```json
{
  "id": "pcsch_1RtBMrPGj7LS2ZC4NtVvHirY",
  "object": "pricing_config_scheme",
  "enabled": true,
  "ends_at": null,
  "livemode": true,
  "pricing_config": "network_costs",
  "starts_at": 1754502193
}
```

This immediately sets the account for network cost passthrough, allowing Stripe to begin passing through network costs to the connected account. If you enable network cost passthrough on an account in the middle of the month, network costs get recovered from the connected account from the time of enablement, not the entire month.

Optionally, to set the account as network cost passthrough at a future date, you can pass the timestamp in the [starts_at](https://docs.stripe.com/api/pricing-config-scheme/create.md?api-version=preview#create_pricing_config_scheme-starts_at) parameter. This determines the time that network costs begin to pass through to the connected account.

You can only create one scheduled scheme at a time for each connected account. If you attempt to create a new scheme while you already have one scheduled, it results in a `400` error. Schemes are immutable, meaning you need to delete and re-create scheduled schemes to make any changes.

You can find current and scheduled schemes in the `Pricing Config` object using the `current_scheme` and `next_scheme` parameters.

```curl
curl -G https://api.stripe.com/v1/pricing_configs/network_costs \
  -u "<<YOUR_SECRET_KEY>>:" \
  -H "Stripe-Version: 2025-07-30.preview; network_costs_private_preview=v1" \
  -H "Stripe-Account: {{CONNECTEDACCOUNT_ID}}" \
  -d "expand[]"=current_scheme \
  -d "expand[]"=next_scheme
```

```json
{
  "id": "network_costs",
  "object": "pricing_config",
  "current_scheme": {
    "id": "pcsch_1RtBSlPGj7LS2ZC4P6VEQe8l",
    "object": "pricing_config_scheme",
    "enabled": false,
    "ends_at": 1754614254,
    "livemode": true,
    "pricing_config": "network_costs",
    "starts_at": 1754502559
  },
  "livemode": true,
  "next_scheme": {
    "id": "pcsch_1RtBhkPGj7LS2ZC4U7LWEvLX",
    "object": "pricing_config_scheme",
    "enabled": true,
    "ends_at": null,
    "livemode": true,
    "pricing_config": "network_costs",
    "starts_at": 1754614254
  }
}
```

### Unset an account as network cost passthrough

You can unset accounts as network cost passthrough by creating a new `network_costs` Pricing Scheme and setting it to [enabled](https://docs.stripe.com/api/pricing-config-scheme/create.md?api-version=preview#create_pricing_config_scheme-enabled) = false.

```curl
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/pricing_configs/network_costs/schemes \
  -u "<<YOUR_SECRET_KEY>>:" \
  -H "Stripe-Version: 2025-07-30.preview; network_costs_private_preview=v1" \
  -H "Stripe-Account: {{CONNECTEDACCOUNT_ID}}" \
  -d enabled=false
```

```json
{
  "id": "pcsch_1RtBSlPGj7LS2ZC4P6VEQe8l",
  "object": "pricing_config_scheme",
  "enabled": false,
  "ends_at": null,
  "livemode": true,
  "pricing_config": "network_costs",
  "starts_at": 1754502559
}
```

After you apply this scheme, Stripe doesn’t charge network costs to the connected account, meaning the account is no longer on network cost passthrough pricing.

To delete a scheduled scheme, use the [DELETE](https://docs.stripe.com/api/pricing-config-scheme/delete.md?api-version=preview) endpoint:

```curl
curl -X DELETE https://api.stripe.com/v1/pricing_configs/network_costs/schemes/pcsch_1RtBWbPGj7LS2ZC4q5lrEuNG \
  -u "<<YOUR_SECRET_KEY>>:" \
  -H "Stripe-Version: 2025-07-30.preview; network_costs_private_preview=v1" \
  -H "Stripe-Account: {{CONNECTEDACCOUNT_ID}}"
```

```json
{
  "id": "pcsch_1RtBWbPGj7LS2ZC4q5lrEuNG",
  "object": "pricing_config_scheme",
  "deleted": true
}
```

You can’t delete a scheme that has a `starts_at` date that’s in the past. If you attempt to do so, Stripe returns a `400` error that prompts you to schedule a new scheme.

### View the network cost passthrough status for an account

The Pricing Config Scheme `current_at` endpoint [returns the pricing scheme](https://docs.stripe.com/api/pricing-config-scheme/retrieve.md?api-version=preview) that you applied at a specific timestamp:

```curl
curl -G https://api.stripe.com/v1/pricing_configs/network_costs/schemes/current_at \
  -u "<<YOUR_SECRET_KEY>>:" \
  -H "Stripe-Version: 2025-07-30.preview; network_costs_private_preview=v1" \
  -H "Stripe-Account: {{CONNECTEDACCOUNT_ID}}" \
  -d current_at=1754502879
```

```json
{
  "id": "pcsch_1RtBSlPGj7LS2ZC4P6VEQe8l",
  "object": "pricing_config_scheme",
  "enabled": true,
  "ends_at": 1754503791,
  "livemode": true,
  "pricing_config": "network_costs",
  "starts_at": 1754502879
}
```

If you call this endpoint with an `current_at` date before the account’s creation date, Stripe returns a `400` error.

## Adjust the application fee for your connected accounts

Connected accounts on blended pricing typically incur higher application fees to cover the underlying network cost, and connected accounts that pay for their own network costs typically pay lower application fees. You can update your pricing logic for application fees in one of two ways:

1. **Update your internal pricing engine**: If you maintain the logic of how much to charge in application fees for each charge and connected account, you need to add the conditional logic in your internal engine to lower the application fees and set the contracted price for a connected account that also pays their own network costs.
1. **Update your pricing in the platform pricing tool**: If you use the [platform pricing tool](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/platform-pricing-tools.md) to execute your application fee pricing strategy, you need to edit your strategy to incorporate differentiated pricing for card payments for users set for network cost passthrough. Typically, the pricing for blended and IC+ priced connected accounts are identical in every aspect except for card payments, where the IC++ connected accounts’ application fee is lower because they’re also paying network costs.

To manage your pricing strategy, we recommend that you:

1. Create a [pricing group](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/platform-pricing-tools/pricing-groups.md) for your IC++ connected accounts.

body:
### Problem

Bitbucket Cloud repository cloning was failing with authentication errors. The root cause was a mismatch between the credential formats required by different Bitbucket operations:

- Bitbucket API calls require the full email address (e.g., `user@example.com`)
- Git clone operations require only the username portion (e.g., user)

Previously, the code was passing the full email address to git clone URLs, causing authentication failures like:

`fatal: Authentication failed for 'https://bitbucket.org/workspace/repo.git'`

### Solution

Extract the username from the configured email address when building git clone URLs for Bitbucket repositories. The fix uses JavaScript's `split('@')[0]` to extract the username portion while maintaining the full email for API authentication.

The `getAuthCredentialsForRepo `function in utils.ts was updated to handle Bitbucket's specific authentication requirements:

1. The full email from config.user is preserved for API operations
2. Only the username portion is used when constructing the `cloneUrlWithToken`
3. The username is passed to `createGitCloneUrlWithToken `which builds the authenticated URL format: `https://username:token@bitbucket.org/...`

### Testing

  - ✅ Verified with Bitbucket Cloud repositories

Resumen:

Inyecta DemoBanner en PublicLayout y DashboardLayout (visible solo con VITE_DEMO_MODE=1).

Normaliza API_BASE y tolera VITE_API_URL/VITE_API_BASE (con auto-sufijo /api).

Corrige la carga pública de establecimientos en BrowsePage usando fetch plano (evita autorización y preflight innecesarios).

Ajustes de CORS (backend) para http://localhost:5173, 5174 y 5175, con credentials: include.

Compatibilidad Vite + React 19 (plugin react con jsxImportSource si aplica).

Cambios principales

frontend/src/components/DemoBanner.jsx (nuevo / mejorado).

frontend/src/layouts/PublicLayout.jsx y DashboardLayout.jsx: inyección del banner.

frontend/src/pages/BrowsePage.jsx: fetch público directo y manejo de loading/errores.

frontend/src/services/apiClient.js: simplificación de llamadas públicas.

frontend/src/api/http.js: normalización robusta de API_BASE.

backend/.env: lista CORS explícita y variables DEMO_.

Cómo probar

Backend:

docker compose up -d --build backend

Verifica preflight:

curl -i -X OPTIONS "http://localhost:5001/api/public/establishments" \
  -H "Origin: http://localhost:5174" \
  -H "Access-Control-Request-Method: GET" \
  -H "Access-Control-Request-Headers: content-type,authorization"


Debe responder 200 con Access-Control-Allow-Origin: http://localhost:5174.

Frontend:

.env con VITE_DEMO_MODE=1 y VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:5001

npm run dev → abre http://localhost:5173 (o 5174/5175 según te salga)

En Inicio, deben listarse los establecimientos sin pedir login; el banner demo visible.

Checklist

 Builds locales OK (backend y frontend).

 CORS verificado en preflight y GET real.

 Navegación pública: listado → booking.

 Banner demo solo cuando VITE_DEMO_MODE=1.

 Sin toasts duplicados ni banners dobles.

Notas

Este PR prepara el terreno para “flujo demo end-to-end” (reserva, reprogramar, cancelar) y evita dependencias de token para endpoints públicos.

Issue(s) relacionado(s)

Closes: demo-mode milestone (si corresponde).

This PR updates [coverage](https://pypi.org/project/coverage) from **5.5** to **7.12.0**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.12.0
   ```
   ---------------------------

- The HTML report now shows separate coverage totals for statements and
  branches, as well as the usual combined coverage percentage. Thanks to Ryuta
  Otsuka for the `discussion <issue 2081_>`_ and the `implementation
  <pull 2085_>`_.

- The JSON report now includes separate coverage totals for statements and
  branches, thanks to `Ryuta Otsuka <pull 2090_>`_.

- Fix: ``except*`` clauses were not handled properly under the "sysmon"
  measurement core, causing KeyError exceptions as described in `issue 2086`_.
  This is now fixed.

- Fix: we now defend against aggressive mocking of ``open()`` that could cause
  errors inside coverage.py.  An example of a failure is in `issue 2083`_.

- Fix: in unusual cases where a test suite intentionally exhausts the system's
  file descriptors to test handling errors in ``open()``, coverage.py would
  fail when trying to open source files, as described in `issue 2091`_.  This
  is now fixed.

- A small tweak to the HTML report: file paths now use thin spaces around
  slashes to make them easier to read.

.. _issue 2081: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2081
.. _issue 2083: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2083
.. _pull 2085: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2085
.. _issue 2086: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2086
.. _pull 2090: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2090
.. _issue 2091: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2091


.. _changes_7-11-3:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.11.3
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: the 7.11.1 changes meant that conflicts between a requested measurement
  core and other settings would raise an error. This was a breaking change from
  previous behavior, as reported in `issue 2076`_ and `issue 2078`_.

  The previous behavior has been restored: when the requested core conflicts
  with other settings, another core is used instead, and a warning is issued.

- For contributors: the repo has moved from Ned's `nedbat GitHub account`_ to
  the `coveragepy GitHub organization`_. The default branch has changed from
  master to main.

.. _changes_7-11-2:

   ### 7.11.2
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: using the "sysmon" measurement core in 7.11.1, if Python code was
  claimed to come from a non-Python file, a ``NotPython`` exception could be
  raised. This could happen for example with Jinja templates compiled to
  Python, as reported in `issue 2077`_. This is now fixed.

- Doc: corrected the first entry in the 7.11.1 changelog.

- Fix: some chanages to details of how the measurement core is chosen, and how
  conflicting settings are handled. The "sysmon" core cannot be used with some
  conurrency settings, with dynamic context, and in Python 3.12/3.13, with
  branch measurement.

  - If the core is not specified and defaults to "sysmon" (Python 3.14+), but
    other settings conflict with sysmon, then the "ctrace" core will be used
    instead with no warning. For concurrency conflicts, this used to produce an
    error, as described in `issue 2064`_.

  - If the "sysmon" core is explicitly requested in your configuration, but
    other settings conflict, an error is now raised. This used to produce a
    warning.

- Fix: some multi-line case clauses or for loops (and probably other
  constructs) could cause incorrect claims of missing branches with the
  sys.monitoring core, as described in `issue 2070`_. This is now fixed.

- Fix: when running in pytest under coverage, a ``breakpoint()`` would stop in
  the wrong frame, one level down from where it should, as described in `issue
  1420`_. This was due to a coverage change in v6.4.1 that seemed to give a
  slight performance improvement, but I couldn't reproduce the performance
  gain, so it's been reverted, fixing the debugger problem.

- A new debug option ``--debug=core`` shows which core is in use and why.

- Split ``sqlite`` debugging information out of the ``sys`` :ref:`coverage
  debug <cmd_debug>` and :ref:`cmd_run_debug` options since it's bulky and not
  very useful.

- Updated the :ref:`howitworks` page to better describe the three different
  measurement cores.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## Overview
Complete integration of Treasury wallet, Towns Protocol SDK, and Direct Messages system for Knead chat.

## 1. Treasury Wallet System

### Create `lib/thirdweb/treasury.ts`
Use ThirdWeb v5 SDK with the following implementation:
```typescript
import { createThirdwebClient, toWei, getTransactionReceipt } from "thirdweb";
import { privateKeyToAccount } from "thirdweb/wallets";
import { base } from "thirdweb/chains";
import { getContract, prepareContractCall, sendTransaction, readContract } from "thirdweb";
import type { Address } from "thirdweb";
```

**Exports:**
- `thirdwebClient` - Created with `THIRDWEB_SECRET_KEY`
- `getTreasuryWallet()` - Returns wallet from `THIRDWEB_PRIVATE_KEY`
- `getTreasuryAddress()` - Returns wallet address as string
- `sendTownsTokens(recipientAddress: Address, amount: string)` - Send ERC20 $TOWNS tokens
  - Uses `toWei(amount, 18)` for precision
  - Uses `getTransactionReceipt()` to get block number
  - Returns `{ transactionHash: string, blockNumber: bigint }`
- `getTreasuryBalance()` - Returns balance as string with 8 decimals

**Error handling:** Throw errors if `THIRDWEB_SECRET_KEY` or `THIRDWEB_PRIVATE_KEY` missing

### Create `app/api/admin/treasury/route.ts`
GET endpoint for Treasury monitoring:
- Verify admin permissions (role = 'admin' or 'emergency_admin')
- Return Treasury address, balance, pending claims, total earnings owed
- Calculate `isHealthy: balance >= totalEarningsOwed`
- Include warning if unhealthy

### Update `app/api/towns/claim/route.ts`
POST endpoint for automated withdrawals:
- Validate user is contributor with sufficient earnings
- Check Treasury has sufficient balance
- Create claim with status 'processing'
- Call `sendTownsTokens()` immediately
- On success: Update claim to 'completed', deduct from user earnings
- On failure: Update claim to 'failed', increment retry_count

## 2. Towns SDK Integration

### Create `lib/towns/client.ts`
Import from '@towns/react' SDK and create wrapper hooks:

**Exports:**
- `useTownsConnection()` - Wraps `useAgentConnection` and `useTownsAuthStatus`
  - Returns: `{ connect, disconnect, isAuthenticated, isConnecting, error }`
  - `connect` accepts Web3 signer from ThirdWeb wallet
  
- `useTownsChannel(channelId: string)` - Wraps `useChannel`
  - Returns: `{ messages, isLoading, error }`
  
- `useTownsSendMessage()` - Wraps `useSendMessage`
  - Returns: `{ sendMessage, isSending, error }`
  - `sendMessage(channelId, content, metadata?)` supports custom metadata
  
- `useTownsReactions(messageId: string)` - Wraps `useReactions`
  - Returns: `{ reactions, addReaction, removeReaction }`
  
- `useTownsThreads(messageId: string)` - Wraps `useThreads`
  - Returns: `{ replies, isLoading }`
  
- Re-export `TownsSyncProvider` from '@towns/react'

Add JSDoc explaining Web3 wallet authentication (no API key needed).

### Create `hooks/useSyncTownsToSupabase.ts`
Hook to sync Towns messages to Supabase for point tracking:
- Import `useTownsChannel` and Supabase client
- Export `useSyncTownsToSupabase(channelId: string)`
- Use `useEffect` to watch for new Towns messages
- For each message:
  - Check if already synced (query by `towns_message_id`)
  - If new, insert into `chat_messages` table:
    - `towns_message_id`: message.id
    - `towns_metadata`: message.metadata (JSONB)
    - `user_id`: message.author.did (or map to your system)
    - `content`, `channel_id`, `created_at`

### Create `app/providers.tsx`
Root provider wrapper:
- 'use client' directive
- Import `TownsSyncProvider` from '@/lib/towns/client'
- Import existing ThirdwebProvider
- Export `Providers({ children })` component:
```tsx
<ThirdwebProvider>
  <TownsSyncProvider>
    {children}
  </TownsSyncProvider>

author: chocapikk
body:
Hello Metasploit Team,

I've created two new exploit modules for Flowise RCE vulnerabilities along with a shared mixin to reduce code duplication and improve maintainability.

## Modules

### 1. flowise_custommcp_rce (CVE-2025-8943)
- **Vulnerability**: Command injection via StdioClientTransport in the customMCP endpoint
- **Affected versions**: >= 2.2.7-patch.1 and < 3.0.1
- **Authentication**: Unauthenticated by default (uses `x-request-from: internal` header). Optional Basic Auth support if `FLOWISE_USERNAME`/`FLOWISE_PASSWORD` environment variables are configured on the target.

### 2. flowise_js_rce (CVE-2025-59528)
- **Vulnerability**: JavaScript injection via `convertToValidJSONString()` using `Function('return ' + inputString)()`
- **Affected versions**: >= 2.2.7-patch.1 and < 3.0.6
- **Authentication**: 
  - Unauthenticated for versions < 3.0.1 (if Basic Auth is not configured)
  - Requires `FLOWISE_EMAIL`/`FLOWISE_PASSWORD` module options for versions >= 3.0.1 (JWT verification introduced)

## Implementation Details

- **Shared mixin**: Created `Msf::Exploit::Remote::HTTP::Flowise` mixin to encapsulate common functionality:
  - Version detection (`flowise_get_version`)
  - Authentication handling (`flowise_login`, `flowise_requires_auth?`)
  - Request sending (`flowise_send_custommcp_request`)

- **Documentation**: Comprehensive documentation with Docker Compose setup for testing multiple Flowise versions simultaneously

## Testing

Successfully tested on:

- **flowise_custommcp_rce (CVE-2025-8943)**:
  - Flowise 2.2.7-patch.1 (unauthenticated, vulnerable)
  - Flowise 2.2.7-patch.1 with Basic Auth configured (FLOWISE_USERNAME/FLOWISE_PASSWORD env vars, vulnerable)
  - Flowise 3.0.0 (unauthenticated, vulnerable)
  - Flowise 3.0.1 (verified fixed, not vulnerable)

- **flowise_js_rce (CVE-2025-59528)**:
  - Flowise 2.2.7-patch.1 (unauthenticated, vulnerable)
  - Flowise 3.0.0 (unauthenticated, vulnerable)
  - Flowise 3.0.4 (authentication required, vulnerable)
  - Flowise 3.0.6 (verified fixed, not vulnerable)

Both vulnerabilities exploit the `/api/v1/node-load-method/customMCP` endpoint, which was introduced in version 2.2.7-patch.1. The endpoint allows execution of OS commands through the Custom MCPs feature, which lacks proper authentication and authorization controls in versions before 3.0.1.

author: copilot
body:
Fixes the `$epacInfoStream` global variable to properly capture all output from `Build-DeploymentPlans` and related deployment scripts.

## Problem
After upgrading to EnterprisePolicyAsCode version 11.0.0 or later, the `$epacInfoStream` variable stopped capturing output because `Write-Information` commands were replaced with `Write-Modern*` functions that use `Write-Host`, which doesn't automatically populate the `InformationVariable`.

## Solution
This PR implements two key changes:

1. **Modified Write-ModernOutput.ps1**: Updated all Write-Modern* functions to append their output to `$Global:epacInfoStream`:
   - `Write-ModernHeader` - captures header output with border characters
   - `Write-ModernSection` - captures section titles and underlines
   - `Write-ModernStatus` - captures status messages with icons
   - `Write-ModernProgress` - captures progress updates
   - `Write-ModernCountSummary` - delegates to other functions

2. **Initialized the global array**: Added `$Global:epacInfoStream = @()` initialization in all scripts that use it:
   - `Scripts/Deploy/Build-DeploymentPlans.ps1`
   - `Scripts/Deploy/Deploy-PolicyPlan.ps1`
   - `Scripts/Deploy/Deploy-RolesPlan.ps1`
   - `Scripts/HydrationKit/Build-HydrationDeploymentPlans.ps1`

## Testing
- ✅ Created and ran comprehensive test script validating output capture
- ✅ Verified all Write-Modern* functions properly append to epacInfoStream
- ✅ Confirmed captured output preserves formatting and special characters
- ✅ All modified files pass PowerShell syntax validation

This fix enables users to capture deployment plan output for PR messages and pipeline summaries as documented.

Fixes #1128

<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.12.0
   ```
   ---------------------------

- The HTML report now shows separate coverage totals for statements and
  branches, as well as the usual combined coverage percentage. Thanks to Ryuta
  Otsuka for the `discussion <issue 2081_>`_ and the `implementation
  <pull 2085_>`_.

- The JSON report now includes separate coverage totals for statements and
  branches, thanks to `Ryuta Otsuka <pull 2090_>`_.

- Fix: ``except*`` clauses were not handled properly under the "sysmon"
  measurement core, causing KeyError exceptions as described in `issue 2086`_.
  This is now fixed.

- Fix: we now defend against aggressive mocking of ``open()`` that could cause
  errors inside coverage.py.  An example of a failure is in `issue 2083`_.

- Fix: in unusual cases where a test suite intentionally exhausts the system's
  file descriptors to test handling errors in ``open()``, coverage.py would
  fail when trying to open source files, as described in `issue 2091`_.  This
  is now fixed.

- A small tweak to the HTML report: file paths now use thin spaces around
  slashes to make them easier to read.

.. _issue 2081: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2081
.. _issue 2083: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2083
.. _pull 2085: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2085
.. _issue 2086: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2086
.. _pull 2090: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2090
.. _issue 2091: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2091


.. _changes_7-11-3:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.11.3
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: the 7.11.1 changes meant that conflicts between a requested measurement
  core and other settings would raise an error. This was a breaking change from
  previous behavior, as reported in `issue 2076`_ and `issue 2078`_.

  The previous behavior has been restored: when the requested core conflicts
  with other settings, another core is used instead, and a warning is issued.

- For contributors: the repo has moved from Ned's `nedbat GitHub account`_ to
  the `coveragepy GitHub organization`_. The default branch has changed from
  master to main.

.. _issue 2076: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2076
.. _issue 2078: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2078
.. _nedbat GitHub account: https://github.com/nedbat
.. _coveragepy GitHub organization: https://github.com/coveragepy


.. _changes_7-11-2:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.11.2
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: using the "sysmon" measurement core in 7.11.1, if Python code was
  claimed to come from a non-Python file, a ``NotPython`` exception could be
  raised. This could happen for example with Jinja templates compiled to
  Python, as reported in `issue 2077`_. This is now fixed.

- Doc: corrected the first entry in the 7.11.1 changelog.

.. _issue 2077: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2077


.. _changes_7-11-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.11.1
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: some chanages to details of how the measurement core is chosen, and how
  conflicting settings are handled. The "sysmon" core cannot be used with some
  conurrency settings, with dynamic context, and in Python 3.12/3.13, with
  branch measurement.

  - If the core is not specified and defaults to "sysmon" (Python 3.14+), but
    other settings conflict with sysmon, then the "ctrace" core will be used
    instead with no warning. For concurrency conflicts, this used to produce an
    error, as described in `issue 2064`_.

  - If the "sysmon" core is explicitly requested in your configuration, but
    other settings conflict, an error is now raised. This used to produce a
    warning.

- Fix: some multi-line case clauses or for loops (and probably other
  constructs) could cause incorrect claims of missing branches with the
  sys.monitoring core, as described in `issue 2070`_. This is now fixed.

- Fix: when running in pytest under coverage, a ``breakpoint()`` would stop in
  the wrong frame, one level down from where it should, as described in `issue
  1420`_. This was due to a coverage change in v6.4.1 that seemed to give a
  slight performance improvement, but I couldn't reproduce the performance
  gain, so it's been reverted, fixing the debugger problem.

- A new debug option ``--debug=core`` shows which core is in use and why.

- Split ``sqlite`` debugging information out of the ``sys`` :ref:`coverage
  debug <cmd_debug>` and :ref:`cmd_run_debug` options since it's bulky and not
  very useful.

- Updated the :ref:`howitworks` page to better describe the three different
  measurement cores.

.. _issue 1420: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1420
.. _issue 2064: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2064
.. _issue 2070: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2070


.. _changes_7-11-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.11.0
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Dropped support for Python 3.9, declared support for Python 3.15 alpha.


.. _changes_7-10-7:
   ```

   ```
   ---------------------------

- Performance: with branch coverage in large files, generating HTML, JSON, or
  LCOV reports could take far too long due to some quadratic behavior when
  creating the function and class index pages.  This is now fixed, closing
  `issue 2048`_.  Thanks to Daniel Diniz for help diagnosing the problem.

- Most warnings and a few errors now have links to a page in the docs

- Fix: ``source`` directories were not properly communicated to subprocesses

author: abc-livraison
body:
# Project Summary: Morty Express Challenge - Group Report

**Group Members:** Anas Maillal, Adnane Alami
**Objective:** Maximize the number of Morties successfully rescued and delivered to Planet Jessica using adaptive decision-making under uncertainty.

## Overview of Approach

Our strategy was built around balancing exploration and exploitation in a non-stationary, partially observable environment. The survival probability on each planet evolves over time as an unknown function—likely composed of multiple periodic components—making static models ineffective. To address this, we designed a dynamic agent that combines Upper Confidence Bound (UCB) action selection with polynomial regression over a rolling buffer to model temporal trends in survival rates.

We began with an epsilon-greedy policy using simple moving averages but quickly transitioned toward UCB-based exploration, which better quantifies uncertainty and ensures systematic exploration of all three planets.

## Key Modeling Insights & Iterations

1.  **Frequency Analysis via FFT (Initial Attempt):** We hypothesized that survival curves were generated by sums of sinusoidal functions. Using the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) on recent outcomes within a fixed-size buffer, we attempted to identify dominant frequencies and predict future survival probabilities. While this provided some insight into periodic patterns, performance plateaued due to phase shifts and frequency changes over time.

2.  **Adaptive Buffer Flushing (Failed RL Extension):** To improve FFT accuracy, we explored dynamically resetting the data buffer when detecting "regime shifts" in survival patterns. We trained a separate reinforcement learning (RL) agent to decide *when* to flush each planet's buffer, with:
    *   **State:** Last N binary survival outcomes.
    *   **Actions:** No flush, or flush one of the three planet buffers.
    *   **Reward:** Survival outcome + penalty for excessive flushing.

    However, despite tuning rewards, the RL agent consistently over-flushed—even with strong negative penalties—leading to poor predictions and low performance. This suggested that learning reliable change-point detection from limited local signals was infeasible without more sophisticated modeling.

3.  **Final Strategy: Polynomial Regression + UCB (Rolling Window):** We abandoned FFT and adopted a simpler yet more effective approach:
    *   Maintain a rolling buffer of the last B trips per planet.
    *   Fit a polynomial of degree d to the survival outcomes over trip numbers in the buffer.
    *   Use the fitted polynomial to predict the next-trip survival rate.
    *   Apply UCB action selection, where the mean estimate is the polynomial prediction, and exploration bonus depends on visit count.

4.  **Trip Sizing Logic:** Although currently set to maximum capacity (3), we implemented logic to scale trip size based on both predicted survival rate and goodness-of-fit (R-squared) of the polynomial. This allows conservative probing when confidence is low.

5.  **Hyperparameter Tuning:** We conducted a grid search over key parameters:
    *   `BUFFER_SIZE`: 50 vs 100
    *   `POLY_DEGREE`: 2 vs 3
    *   `UCB_C`: 1.5, 2.0, 2.5
    *   `INITIAL_EXPLORATION_TRIPS`: 5 or 10

Our implementation includes full logging, progress visualization, and plotting tools to analyze:
- Survival trends
- Moving averages
- Polynomial predictions vs actual outcomes
- Risk evolution over time

## Code Structure & Usage

```bash
python morty_poly_reg.py             # Run default agent
python morty_poly_reg.py tune     # Run hyperparameter tuning
python morty_poly_reg.py 5          # Run 5 episodes

body:
Implements full movie details modal displaying TMDB data (cast, crew, reviews, recommendations, budget, keywords) when clicking movie cards.

## Changes

### Modal Infrastructure
- Added modal container with overlay, close button, and content area to `index.html`
- Implemented modal lifecycle: open/close via button, overlay click, or ESC key
- Body scroll lock when modal active

### API Integration
Six parallel fetch functions for optimal performance:
```javascript
const [details, credits, reviews, videos, recommendations, keywords] = 
  await Promise.all([
    fetchMovieDetails(movieId),
    fetchMovieCredits(movieId),
    fetchMovieReviews(movieId),
    fetchMovieVideos(movieId),
    fetchMovieRecommendations(movieId),
    fetchMovieKeywords(movieId)
  ]);
```

### UI Components (~600 lines CSS)
- **Header**: Backdrop image, poster, title, color-coded rating circle (green ≥70%, yellow ≥40%, red <40%), genres, runtime
- **Cast**: Horizontal scrolling cards with actor photos and character names (top 10)
- **Reviews**: User reviews with avatars and dates (up to 3)
- **Recommendations**: Clickable related movies with recursive navigation
- **Additional Info**: Budget, revenue, keywords, original title, status

### Click Integration
```javascript
card.addEventListener('click', () => openMovieDetails(id));
card.style.cursor = 'pointer';
```

Applied to all movie cards (trending, popular, trailers).

## Responsive Design
- Desktop: Full layout with 300px poster
- Mobile: Stacked layout with adjusted sizing

body:
## Plan for pipr improvements

- [ ] 1. macOS/Bash 3.2 portability - Replace mapfile with portable fallback
  - [ ] Create helper function to capture URLs (use mapfile when available, otherwise while read loop)
  - [ ] Apply helper to both verbose and non-verbose branches (lines 176 and 178)
- [ ] 2. YTDLP_FORMAT override and logging enhancements
  - [ ] Make YTDLP_FORMAT overridable via environment variable (default: bestvideo*+bestaudio/best)
  - [ ] Log the chosen YTDLP_FORMAT
  - [ ] Log number of resolved URLs
  - [ ] Log whether explicit stream mapping (0:v + 1:a) is being applied
- [ ] 3. Robustness and exit visibility
  - [ ] Add set -E to preserve ERR trap behavior
  - [ ] Add EXIT trap to log exit status code
  - [ ] Keep existing set -e and function-local set +e
- [ ] 4. Add optional --pixfmt flag
  - [ ] Add flag to argument parser
  - [ ] Apply to encoding function
  - [ ] Update help text
- [ ] 5. Test and verify all changes
- [ ] 6. Run code review
- [ ] 7. Run CodeQL security check

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> Summary
> Improve portability and ergonomics of the pipr script while keeping behavior backward compatible.
> 
> Scope of work
> 1) macOS/Bash 3.2 portability
> - Problem: macOS ships Bash 3.2 which lacks mapfile/readarray; current code will fail there.
> - Change: Implement a portable fallback for capturing yt-dlp output into MEDIA_URLS when mapfile is not available. Apply to both verbose and non-verbose branches.
> - Suggested approach: encapsulate URL capture in a helper that uses mapfile when present, otherwise loops with while IFS= read -r line; do MEDIA_URLS+=("$line"); done.
> 
> 2) YTDLP_FORMAT override and logging niceties
> - Make YTDLP_FORMAT overridable via environment variable, defaulting to bestvideo*+bestaudio/best.
> - Log the chosen YTDLP_FORMAT.
> - After resolving MEDIA_URLS, log the number of URLs and whether explicit stream mapping (0:v + 1:a) is being applied.
> 
> 3) Robustness and exit visibility
> - Add set -E to preserve ERR trap behavior and add a simple EXIT trap to log exit status code for better post-mortems. Keep existing set -e behavior and function-local set +e around ffmpeg runs.
> 
> 4) Optional encoder compatibility flag
> - Add a new optional flag --pixfmt <fmt> that, when provided, appends -pix_fmt <fmt> during re-encoding. This helps compatibility with some RTMP targets that require yuv420p.
> 
> Files to modify
> - pipr (script)
> - README.md (documentation)
> 
> Detailed acceptance criteria
> - On macOS (Bash 3.2), running pipr -h works and the yt-dlp URL capture code path does not reference mapfile when it is unavailable.
> - YTDLP_FORMAT is set as: YTDLP_FORMAT=${YTDLP_FORMAT:-bestvideo*+bestaudio/best} and the script logs the chosen format on startup.
> - The script logs: (a) the count of MEDIA_URLS returned and (b) whether mapping for separate A/V will be applied.
> - When --pixfmt yuv420p is provided, the encode path includes -pix_fmt yuv420p.
> - README reflects the environment override and the new --pixfmt flag, and includes a short note about macOS Bash 3.2 compatibility.
> 
> Implementation notes
> - Be careful not to change default behavior: copy-first fallback to re-encode remains unchanged.
> - Preserve sanitizer behavior and logging, including process substitution for stderr filtering.
> - Keep options parsing style consistent with existing code.
> 
> Suggested test plan
> - Linux: Run pipr against a public VOD and live HLS with: copy-first success and forced encode.
> - macOS (Bash 3.2): Verify -h and a dry run that reaches yt-dlp execution path without mapfile errors (e.g., by pointing at a valid URL and quickly interrupting).
> - Verify YTDLP_FORMAT override works by exporting YTDLP_FORMAT and checking the logged format line.
> - Verify --pixfmt yuv420p shows up in the ffmpeg command line during encode.
> 
> Non-goals for this PR
> - Adding generic pass-through args for yt-dlp/ffmpeg and extended protocol sanitization can be considered in a separate PR.


</details>

  - /payment/success: Success confirmation page
  - /payment/failed: Failed payment page
- Added environment variables for Razorpay configuration
- Created comprehensive documentation (PAYMENT_INTEGRATION.md)

Features:
- Secure payment processing with signature verification
- Database tracking of all payment transactions
- Support for linking payments to tourists and requests
- Customizable discovery fee amount via environment variable
- Auto-redirect after successful payment
- Test and production mode support

The default discovery fee is set to ₹99 (configurable via DISCOVERY_FEE_AMOUNT env variable).

body:
This commit adds a complete development ecosystem for PIPER on Tenstorrent Greyskull, including examples, benchmarks, automation, testing, and documentation.

## Working Examples (examples/)

Python Examples:
- neg2zero_pipeline.py: Stateless Neg2Zero operator with validation and benchmarking
- vocab_mapper.py: Stateful VocabMap operator with SRAM analysis

C++ Kernels:
- kernels/neg2zero_kernel.cpp: TT-Metalium low-level implementation
- kernels/CMakeLists.txt: Build system for C++ kernels

## Automation Scripts (scripts/)

- install.sh: Master installation script with dependency management
- setup_hugepages.sh: HugePages configuration with systemd service
- verify_installation.sh: Comprehensive installation verification

Features:
- Error handling and recovery
- Progress indicators
- Detailed logging
- Rollback support

## Benchmark Suite (benchmark/)

- criteo_preprocessing.py: Comprehensive benchmark for all PIPER operators
  * Stateless: Neg2Zero, Logarithm, Modulus
  * Stateful: VocabMap
  * JSON output for results
  * CPU baseline comparison

## Testing Infrastructure (tests/)

- test_operators.py: Unit tests for preprocessing operators
- pytest configuration
- Coverage support

## Monitoring Tools (monitoring/)

- monitor.py: Real-time device metrics monitoring
  * Temperature tracking
  * Power consumption
  * Memory usage
  * JSON export

## Docker Support

- Dockerfile: Multi-stage build for optimized images
  * Base system dependencies
  * TT-Metal SDK build
  * TT-Buda framework
  * PIPER application layer

- docker-compose.yml: Orchestration with multiple services
  * Main PIPER service
  * Benchmark runner
  * Development environment with Jupyter
  * Monitoring service
  * Testing service

## Documentation (docs/)

- architecture.md: Deep-dive into PIPER on Greyskull
  * Hardware layout diagrams
  * Software stack layers
  * Memory hierarchy
  * Data flow
  * Performance characteristics

- operators.md: Complete operator reference
  * Stateless operators (Neg2Zero, Logarithm, Modulus)
  * Stateful operators (VocabMap, VocabGen)
  * Performance metrics
  * Usage examples
  * Composition patterns

- performance.md: Performance tuning guide
  * Optimization checklist
  * Common issues and solutions
  * Tuning techniques
  * Benchmarking best practices
  * Profiling tools

- migration.md: Greyskull → Wormhole/Blackhole migration
  * Hardware replacement steps
  * Software update procedures
  * Code changes required
  * Compatibility matrix
  * Rollback plan

## Dependencies

- requirements.txt: Python package dependencies
  * PyTorch ecosystem
  * Data processing (numpy, pandas, pyarrow)
  * Testing (pytest, pytest-cov)
  * Code quality (black, flake8, mypy)
  * Development tools (jupyter, ipython)

## File Permissions

All scripts and Python files made executable:
- scripts/*.sh
- examples/*.py
- benchmark/*.py
- monitoring/*.py

## Project Structure

```
PIPER/
├── benchmark/          # Performance benchmarking
├── docs/              # Technical documentation
├── examples/          # Working code examples
│   └── kernels/       # C++ TT-Metalium kernels
├── monitoring/        # Real-time monitoring tools
├── scripts/           # Installation and automation
├── tests/             # Unit and integration tests
│   ├── unit/
│   └── integration/
├── Dockerfile         # Container image
├── docker-compose.yml # Orchestration
├── requirements.txt   # Python dependencies
└── readme.md          # Main documentation (updated previously)
```

## Testing

All components have been structured for easy testing:
- Unit tests for operators
- Integration tests for pipelines
- Benchmark validation
- Installation verification

## Usage

Quick start:
```bash
# Automated installation
sudo ./scripts/install.sh

# Verify
./scripts/verify_installation.sh

# Run examples

body:
During recent command testing, I experimented with the setup command and forgot to remove `otel_runtime.go`. This leftover file caused the following generic error:

Error:
[0] failed to run build plan: exit status 1
Stack: ...


Because this message is not very informative, it can be confusing for users (this of course can be any other error). The actual underlying issue is visible only in the build log so I was thinking about emitting more detailed message by reading it from `build-plan.log`:
```
Error:
[0] failed to run build plan: 
otel.runtime.go:7:8: no required module provides package github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/pkg/instrumentation/grpc; to add it:
	go get github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/pkg/instrumentation/grpc
otel.runtime.go:8:8: no required module provides package github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/pkg/instrumentation/nethttp; to add it:
	go get github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/pkg/instrumentation/nethttp
: exit status 1

Stack:
```

Alternatively, at minimum, we could enhance the error message to point users to the log file, for example:
```
[0] failed to run build plan: exit status 1 — see build-plan.log for details.
```
Third option of course is to leave as it is.

I'm leaving the final approach to your judgement/consideration.

author: ctdax
body: #### PR description: This pull request introduces the ability to decay R-hadrons during simulation using a side instance of Pythia8. A generator is required to decay the underlying SUSY particle to hadronize the outgoing partons. This will allow users to simulate detector interactions of long-lived R-hadrons with proper decays for the first time. [See the talk given here.](https://indico.cern.ch/event/1613012/#76-r-hadron-decays) ##### How to use it - Create a SLHA decay table that includes the decays and widths of the underlying SUSY particle in the R-hadron, e.g. the gluino or the stop. - Pass the SLHA decay table to `SLHAFileForPythia8` inside of process.generator or process.g4SimHits in the python config file. Optionally, commands can be passed directly to the instance of pythia that handles the R-hadron decay via `RhadronPythiaDecayerCommandFile`, e.g. ```python process.generator = cms.EDFilter("Pythia8ConcurrentGeneratorFilter", SLHAFileForPythia8 = cms.string('SimG4Core/CustomPhysics/data/TESTDECAY_GLUINO1800_STOP500.txt'), RhadronPythiaDecayerCommandFile = cms.untracked.string('SimG4Core/CustomPhysics/data/RhadronPythiaDecayerCommands.txt'), ... ) ``` - Make sure the event generator doesn't decay the SUSY particle before it is handed to Geant for simulation. If the event generator is pythia, you can force the SUSY particle to not decay via `pythia8CommonSettings` in the python config file: ```python process.generator = cms.EDFilter("Pythia8ConcurrentGeneratorFilter", PythiaParameters = cms.PSet( pythia8CommonSettings = cms.vstring( '1000021:mayDecay = off' ) ) ) ``` ##### Explanation of changes - **RHadronPythiaDecayer.cc/RHadronPythiaDecayer.h:** Utilizes G4Decay::DecayIt() to decay the R-hadron. Because it is defined as an external decayer, when G4Decay::DecayIt() calls ImportDecayProducts() it calls the function inside of RHadronPythiaDecayer. This file strips the incoming R-hadron down to its constituents, decays the underlying SUSY particle, then lets Pythia handle the hadronization. The decay products are returned to G4Decay::DecayIt() for them to be simulated in Geant. - **SimG4Core/CustomPhysics/python/Exotica_HSCP_SIM_cfi.py:** Handles the inputs `SLHAFileForPythia8` and `RhadronPythiaDecayerCommandFile`. Automatically produces and keeps the GenPlusSimParticle collection. - **SimG4Core/CustomPhysics/src/CustomParticleFactory.cc:** Forces the lifetime of R-hadrons to match the lifetime of their underlying SUSY particle, which is read in from the SLHA table. The modification to Line298 `if ((ToLower(line).find("block") < line.npos) || (line == "#")) {` forces the skipping of commented lines in the SLHA text file. - **SimG4Core/CustomPhysics/src/CustomPhysicsList.cc:** Sets the R-hadron decay process to be the external pythia decayer. - **SimG4Core/CustomPhysics/data/RhadronPythiaDecayerCommands.txt:** A new .txt file that contains default commands for the Pythia instance that decays the Rhadrons. - **SimG4Core/CustomPhysics/python/CustomPhysics_cfi.py:** Adds the `RhadronPythiaDecayerCommandFile` parameter to the config file. - **PhysicsTools/HepMCCandAlgos/plugins/GenPlusSimParticleProducer.cc‎:** A special case if statement needed to be added to the producer to add the R-hadron decay products to the collection in the scenario where the R-hadron has a small ctau. Because of how the producer works, the decay products of the R-hadron would only be added to the collection if the R-hadron first flipped types before decaying. This does not often happen when the ctau of the R-hadron is small. - **SimG4Core/CustomPhysics/BuildFile.xml‎:** Add pythia interface for the RHadronPythiaDecayer. ##### Confirmation of 4-momentum conservation at the decay A histogram plotting the difference in 4-momentum between the R-hadron and its decay products in 50 events is shown below. These are the 4-momenta in the $p_T$, $\eta$, $\phi$ basis after the decay products are handed back to Geant. All entries are consistent with 0 difference except for some floating-point error. #### PR validation: All tests below ran successfully. ```bash cd src scram b distclean git cms-checkdeps -a -A scram b -j 8 scram b runtests use-ibeos runTheMatrix.py -l limited -i all --ibeos ``` Before submitting your pull requests, make sure you followed this checklist: - verify that the PR is really intended for the chosen branch - verify that changes follow [CMS Naming, Coding, And Style Rules](http://cms-sw.github.io/cms_coding_rules.html) - verify that the PR passes the basic test procedure suggested in the [CMSSW PR instructions](https://cms-sw.github.io/PRWorkflow.html)
